edges.effect_quant: In Taiwan's nationwide follow-up, birth-dose hepatitis B vaccination was associated with an age- and sex-adjusted relative risk of 0.31 for hepatocellular carcinoma compared with unvaccinated birth cohorts.
edges.population: birth cohorts receiving hepatitis B vaccination starting at birth
edges.mechanism: The vaccine prevents chronic perinatal hepatitis B infection, cutting off one of the dominant causal pathways leading from early HBV acquisition to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma in childhood and early adulthood.
edges.summary: This is one of the strongest cancer-prevention vaccine stories in medicine. Long-term Taiwanese follow-up shows that hepatitis B vaccination beginning at birth sharply lowers later childhood and young-adult hepatocellular carcinoma incidence.
edges.caveats: Residual cancer risk remains highest in children born to highly infectious mothers or those who do not complete the vaccine series. The edge reflects population-level prevention rather than guaranteed individual elimination of risk.

evidence.citation: ChangMH et al 2009 J Natl Cancer Inst
evidence.notes: Decreased incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in hepatitis B vaccinees: a 20-year follow-up study.
